summary: Record the first executable controller skeleton as a cross-cutting behavioral implementation change requiring full five-stage review before further implementation proceeds.
reason: Revision 3 Adversarial revalidation found that WorkflowDefinition and OperationResult still trusted Python annotations at runtime, allowing malformed or mutable workflow definitions and result envelopes outside the closed machine-readable taxonomy. Revision 4 adds deterministic runtime validation for all declared fields on those exposed boundaries, rejects raw stage arguments at workflow traversal, and adds focused regression coverage. Because these corrections tighten controller-owned workflow and result contract boundaries, the review reopens at Adversarial and the full five-stage program remains required before implementation may continue beyond the skeleton.

reasons: This execution unit covers only the revision-4 Adversarial revalidation of the corrected controller-core skeleton; the other four semantic stages remain separate later execution units.

The corrected governed surface remains small and cohesive enough to retest failure, replay, authority-bypass, mutation, stale-state, representability, and recovery risks in one bounded Adversarial pass.

workload.notes: Revision-4 full-program Adversarial revalidation under SEPARATED execution; no semantic stage credit is created by this gate.

capability.benchmark_evidence: Built-in separated default; not a claim of measured reviewer capability.

decision.assurance_boundary: Semantic judgment determines whether one pass is suitable and which bounded subpasses require isolation. Deterministic policy defaults to SEPARATED, converts declared isolation requirements into ISOLATED subpasses, and permits FUSED only through exact pre-existing VALIDATED capability permission. The gate and completion validator enforce the recorded plan but do not prove the semantic assessment itself was correct.

findings: BLOCKING: The persistence DTO boundary still trusts Python annotations at runtime. AuthoritativeRecord, InitializationCommit, TransitionCommit, CreateResult, and TransitionResult accept wrong-typed values without deterministic rejection, including raw/non-StateSnapshot state values, raw IDs, non-bool created/committed flags, and mutable list containers for fields declared as immutable tuples. This lets malformed or mutable authority/evidence representations cross the backend-neutral persistence boundary despite the frozen typed/immutable protocol contract.
evidence: Issue #11 Slice 1 persistence protocol/DTO and immutable evidence requirements
unresolved_conditions: Do not advance to Interdependency. Add deterministic runtime validation for every declared field on the exposed persistence DTOs: require StateSnapshot/typed identity instances where declared, real bool values for created/committed, and immutable tuple containers for immutable history/events/evidence. Add focused regression coverage for wrong-typed state/identity/boolean values and mutable tuple-field containers; record the correction, increment review_revision, regenerate the queue, and reopen Adversarial against the corrected governed target.
